subsystems.name: Ribbon
subsystems.role: the load-bearing tether that extends from the equator past geostationary altitude.
parts: protective coating against atomic oxygen and ultraviolet light

subsystems.name: Base anchor
subsystems.role: holds the lower end of the ribbon and lets climbers start their ascent.

subsystems.name: Counterweight and apex station
subsystems.role: provides the outward pull that keeps the ribbon taut.

subsystems.name: Climbers
subsystems.role: carry payloads up and down the ribbon using electric drive.

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: supplies energy to climbers without heavy onboard fuel.

subsystems.name: Tracking, control and repair
subsystems.role: protects the ribbon from debris and repairs damage.

buildSteps.title: Make the tether material
buildSteps.detail: Synthesise nanotubes with very few defects, then spin them into fibres and composite strands. The challenge is growing them long enough and strong enough while keeping the structure nearly perfect.

buildSteps.title: Qualify the ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Test candidate strands for tensile strength, fatigue, ultraviolet degradation, atomic-oxygen erosion and micrometeoroid impact. Develop coatings and sacrificial outer layers.

buildSteps.title: Launch a seed ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Use existing rockets to place a small seed ribbon and a counterweight in geostationary orbit. Deploy one end downward toward the equator and the other outward beyond geostationary altitude.

buildSteps.title: Anchor and tension
buildSteps.detail: Attach the lower end to an equatorial ocean platform. Adjust the counterweight mass or position until the ribbon is held taut by the outward centrifugal pull.

buildSteps.title: Build and test climbers
buildSteps.detail: Design lightweight electric climbers that grip the ribbon and climb at modest speed. Test them first on short suspended tethers or subscale in-orbit ribbons.

buildSteps.title: Deploy power beaming
buildSteps.detail: Install a ground-based laser or microwave array that tracks each climber and delivers power to its receiver, avoiding the mass penalty of carrying all energy onboard.

buildSteps.title: Scale up capacity
buildSteps.detail: Send climbers up with additional strands and attach them to the seed ribbon. Repeat over years to thicken the ribbon and raise its payload capacity.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Track orbital debris, route climbers around damaged sections, send repair robots to fix or replace strands, and eventually build a second ribbon for redundancy.

prerequisites.why: no fibre yet combines the required strength, stiffness, length and reliability at engineering scale.
large objects are tracked, but small debris and meteoroids cannot yet be predicted or avoided reliably.
laser and microwave power transfer has been demonstrated at short range, not at the power and distance a climber needs.
needed to deploy, thicken and repair the ribbon without sending crews for every task.
existing rockets can place the seed ribbon and counterweight, though at high cost and low mass.

pathway.milestone: metre-scale nanotube fibres with strength and stiffness close to theoretical limits
pathway.unlocks: a credible candidate material for a ribbon.

pathway.milestone: deploy a tether a few kilometres long from a small satellite or suborbital platform and climb it
pathway.unlocks: confidence in deployment, climbing and survival against the space environment.

pathway.milestone: place a low-capacity seed ribbon from geostationary orbit to the equator and lift small payloads
pathway.unlocks: non-rocket access to geostationary orbit, even if limited in mass.

pathway.milestone: use climbers to add strands and build power-beaming infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: rising payload capacity toward routine cargo and crew transport.

pathway.milestone: multiple ribbons at different equatorial sites with repair and redundancy
pathway.unlocks: low-cost surface-to-orbit transport and large space infrastructure.
